raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`SGLANG_K3_SP_ATTN_RES` keeps post-MoE residual streams and bank operations on each rank's token shard, then gathers the normalized attention input. Its eligibility check also requires K3's custom collective backend, preventing NCCL deployments from using an existing layout that already has ordinary ReduceScatter/AllGather fallbacks.

## Modifications

- Remove the custom-collective requirement from bank-slice eligibility. Preserve the existing opt-in switch, SP-MoE and residual-bank requirements, PP=1 restriction, consecutive-MoE guard, and speculative hidden-state capture exclusions.
- Keep fused bank/communication paths conditional on custom collective availability. At the terminal bank read, skip custom fusion preparation when no custom gather callback exists; this avoids preparing a pending residual add only to fall back to the ordinary read.
- Use the actual eligibility helper throughout the stage-planning tests, including the terminal read, and check NCCL fallback behavior without a custom communicator.
- Update the existing switch's documentation. No new flags, device-name checks, private communicators, tuning-table bypasses, or communication kernels are introduced.

This reduces the bank rows read and written; it does not shrink the physical bank allocation. The contiguous-QKV convolution optimization is independent and is not included in either measurement arm.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated revision `34f21eebabbcf8130d6adb331f289f7b88a1e8c9` against common base `17e94c4677d7beb58a89b104fd61b3768994e45e`:

- CPU stage-planning and bank-residual suites: **17 passed, 27 subtests**. Tests exercise the real eligibility helper, ordinary NCCL boundary moves, custom-collective fallbacks, terminal output ownership, and rejection of stale full-bank reads.
- The terminal-read regression checks that NCCL-only execution never enters custom fusion preparation while a supplied custom gather still permits a fusion attempt.
- isort, Ruff formatting and repository-configured lint rules, registered-test lint, AST parsing, and `git diff --check` passed.

<!-- accuracy-results:start -->
Real-routing model regression on B300: ISL 257/4096 with OSL 16 and ISL 65536 with OSL 1, each repeated twice. All 66 generated token IDs and their per-step top-20 token IDs/logprobs match the common baseline exactly (maximum absolute logprob difference 0). Repeated probes within each arm also match exactly. These synthetic regression probes are not a task-accuracy benchmark.
<!-- accuracy-results:end -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Independent baseline and PR worktrees use the same common base above. Conditions: Kimi-K3, 8× B300 (B30Z/SM103), TP8/EP8, MegaMoE with default real expert routing, ISL 65,536, OSL 1, concurrency 1, chunk 65,536, BF16 recurrent state, FP8 KV, `NCCL_SYM_CTAS=16`, default CE AllGather, MegaMoE reserved SMs=2. CUDA graphs, radix caching, overlap scheduling, custom SP collectives, and AR fusion are disabled. Only the PR arm enables the existing bank shard carry switch.

Each independent restart receives 4 warmup requests and two 16-request measured blocks. Baseline and PR are measured twice in an interleaved baseline/KDA/bank sequence. No profiler or hot-path diagnostic code is attached. Throughput is total input tokens divided by total measured duration; P50/P99 are recomputed from all raw formal requests in each row.

The original explicit `fake` dispatch fails on the common base because Kimi-K3 does not provide expert placement metadata. Both arms therefore use the default real routing. These results are not combined with the earlier prototype's fake-dispatch measurements.

<!-- performance-results:start -->
| Configuration | Requests | Input tok/s | P50 TTFT (s) | P99 TTFT (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline R1 | 32 | 35,164.43 | 1.863768 | 1.873641 |
| bank R1 | 32 | 36,691.76 | 1.785341 | 1.802436 |
| baseline R2 | 32 | 35,200.97 | 1.859663 | 1.895896 |
| bank R2 | 32 | 36,623.06 | 1.785267 | 1.840323 |
| baseline pooled | 64 | 35,182.69 | 1.861480 | 1.886303 |
| bank pooled | 64 | 36,657.38 | 1.785341 | 1.829465 |

Across 64 formal requests per arm, input throughput changes by **+4.19%** and P50 TTFT falls by **76.138 ms**. All formal requests succeed with zero cache hits and zero retractions. These measurements describe the complete PR relative to the common base; they do not isolate the incremental review edits.
<!-- performance-results:end -->

## Checklist

- [x] Preserve the existing feature gate and parallelism restrictions.
- [x] Reuse the existing NCCL fallbacks and extend registered tests.
- [x] Avoid custom fusion preparation on the NCCL terminal path.
- [x] Complete exact-revision real-routing model regression and serving measurements.
- [ ] Run upstream GPU CI after maintainer approval.

<!-- pr-states:start -->
---
### CI States

Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #41082304711](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41082304711)<!-- slot:pr-test:end -->
Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #41082304940](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41082304940)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->
Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #41082304629](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41082304629)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end -->
<!-- pr-states:end -->
